title: wg: tier provider-auth and calls, and extract the replacement text as PRs
description:
Mark asked (2026-11-26) to run the SHOULD/MAY tiering lens over
draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth and draft-atwood-mimi-calls, as bead
mimid-1wgh.37.104.15 did for catch-up. Both read for this.

## The pattern Mark already has

Both existing drafts carry a section of paste-ready text for a WG
document:

- provider-auth §"Replacement Text for the MIMI Protocol": replaces
  protocol-07 §4.1's "The TLS connection ... MUST be mutually
  authenticated" paragraph.
- calls §"Replacement Text for MIMI Content": text to add to
  mimi-content §5.10 after the sentence putting calling out of scope.

So the tiering was already being done by hand, inside each draft. The
move is to EXTRACT those sections and propose them as small PRs, which
shrinks each draft to the mechanism it actually defines.

draft-atwood-mimi-catchup has no such section. That is a gap in it, not
a difference in kind: it should get one for protocol-07 §5.5, carrying
tier 1 of mimid-1wgh.37.104.15.

## provider-auth: least dissolvable, MUST stay a draft

Needs a document, and this is a hard constraint, not a preference:

- It defines a DNS TXT record format: the `_mimi` owner name, ABNF,
  `v=MIMI1` with k and p tags. That is a new format, not guidance.
- It requests TWO IANA registrations in registries MIMI does not own,
  each needing a stable reference: `_mimi` in the Underscored and
  Globally Scoped DNS Node Names registry (RFC 8552), and the `mimi`
  service name (RFC 6335). A PR against protocol-07 cannot carry these
  unless protocol-07 itself defines the record.
- The RFC 9421 signing and verifying profile is substantial.

But two pieces come out as PRs, and the first is the valuable one:

1. §4.1's replacement text. protocol-07 currently MANDATES mutually
   authenticated TLS. That mandate is the actual problem: it is why
   mimid cannot claim conformance (AGENTS.md) and why coland interop
   uses RFC 9421 signatures instead (bead mimid-1wgh.46.11.2). Landing
   only the softening -- the target authenticates the source by one of
   several mechanisms, which it accepts being local policy -- removes a
   false mandate for EVERY implementation, with no obligation to adopt
   the DNS-key mechanism at all. Highest value per word of any of this.
2. RFC 6125 -> RFC 9525. protocol-07 cites an obsoleted RFC. That is an
   erratum, uncontroversial, and free. Worth sending on its own so it
   cannot be held up by anything else.

No meaningful tier 2.

## calls: most dissolvable, may not need to be a draft

- NO NEW WIRE AT ALL. The media secret is derived with
  mls-extensions SafeExportSecret under a component id and a label. No
  new structs, no new fields; it is a computation rule plus rekeying
  rules plus the analysis of when it is safe.
- Its one IANA ask is an entry in the MIMI App Component registry, which
  protocol-07 §10 establishes -- a registry MIMI owns. Unlike `_mimi`,
  this can be registered BY protocol-07 itself, so it needs no separate
  referenceable document.
- Its §5.10 replacement text is already written.

So calls could plausibly become two PRs: the mimi-content §5.10 text,
and a registration of media_keys in protocol-07 §10 carrying the
derivation and rekeying rules, with §"Why the Group Secret Is Not Always
the Call Secret" folded in as a security consideration.

Against dissolving it: a registration plus a derivation plus rekeying
plus the subset-call analysis is a document's worth of text even with no
new bytes, and the WG may prefer a short draft to a large PR. But of the
three this is the one where "not a draft" is a real option, which
confirms the guess in mimid-1wgh.37.14 -- now from the content and not
from the size.

## The order this suggests

Smallest and most separable first, so nothing valuable waits on
anything contested:

1. RFC 6125 -> RFC 9525 in protocol-07. Free.
2. provider-auth §4.1 softening. Unblocks implementations that do not
   do mTLS, including mimid.
3. catch-up tier 1 (mimid-1wgh.37.104.15): the honesty requirement and
   the fanout-to-every-provider clarification in §5.5.
4. calls: the mimi-content §5.10 text.
5. Then the mechanisms, as drafts: provider-auth (must be), catchUp
   (the endpoint), and calls only if the PRs do not carry it.

Nothing upstream without Mark's OK (memory: dont-flood-upstream), and no
JMAP in any of it (AGENTS.md).
